victim.name: Eleanor Voss
victim.note: Disappeared at sea; body never recovered.

suspects.name: Adrian Voss
suspects.note: Survives the voyage; last known person with Eleanor; stands to benefit financially from her death.

suspects.name: Marcus Voss
suspects.note: Complicated relationship with Eleanor; disputed parts of the family estate.

suspects.name: Daniel Mercer
suspects.note: Performed maintenance before the voyage; claims everything was properly repaired.

evidence.name: Harbor Departure Record
evidence.description: Establishes the voyage's departure time and passengers.

evidence.name: Weather Report
evidence.description: Confirms deteriorating conditions during the voyage; supports the accident theory on its own.

evidence.name: Repair Records
evidence.description: Establishes boat maintenance performed before the voyage.

evidence.name: Mechanic Statement
evidence.description: Daniel Mercer's account of the repair; introduces a contradiction with the recorded work.

evidence.name: Financial Records
evidence.description: Establishes possible motive tied to Adrian's account access.

evidence.name: Estate Document
evidence.description: Shows inheritance changes Eleanor was preparing before the voyage.

evidence.name: Account-Access Records
evidence.description: Links Adrian directly to the financial motive.

evidence.name: Family History
evidence.description: Eleanor's father died years earlier under natural circumstances; Adrian had previously asked about that estate. A deliberate red herring tempting the player toward an unsupported pattern.

evidence.name: Damage Pattern
evidence.description: Physical damage inconsistent with simple mechanical failure; challenges the accident theory.

evidence.name: Original Repair Documentation
evidence.description: Reveals the opportunity window for sabotage.

evidence.name: Emergency Communication Log
evidence.description: Contradicts the timing in Adrian's account.

evidence.name: Eleanor's Private Note
evidence.description: Shows Eleanor suspected Adrian of financial irregularities before the voyage.

evidence.name: Adrian's Rescue Statement
evidence.description: Adrian's initial account of the sinking; true but incomplete.

evidence.name: Adrian's Revised Statement
evidence.description: A later, deceptive revision that provides the final contradiction against Adrian's original account.

puzzles.name: Voyage Timeline & Repair Reconstruction
puzzles.description: Reconstruct the sequence of departure, weather deterioration, engine trouble, emergency communication, evacuation, and rescue, then determine who repaired what, when, and why — the records contain an inconsistency between recorded and actual work.

puzzles.name: Financial Investigation & Family History
puzzles.description: Examine financial records, estate changes, and account-access history to establish possible motive, then investigate the grandfather/estate pattern — this is designed to tempt the player toward an unsupported conclusion.

puzzles.name: Damage Analysis
puzzles.description: Examine the damage pattern and determine whether it is consistent with a simple mechanical failure.

puzzles.name: Communication Timeline & Eleanor's Hidden Information
puzzles.description: Compare Adrian's emergency communication timing with his account, then discover information indicating Eleanor suspected Adrian of financial irregularities.

puzzles.name: Adrian's Contradictions & Final Reconstruction
puzzles.description: Compare Adrian's initial and revised statements, identify inconsistencies, and assemble the final reasoning.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: If the player quickly identifies Adrian as suspicious, the AI can encourage examination of the family-history pattern, creating a confirmation-bias trap.
puzzles.design_constraint: The player may identify the correct suspect but should still receive a weaker reasoning score if the explanation is unsupported; conversely, credit should be given for correctly identifying what the evidence cannot establish (the exact mechanism/moment of Eleanor's death).

hypotheses.statement: The boat suffered an accident and Eleanor died as a result.
Someone other than Adrian deliberately damaged the boat.
Adrian deliberately sabotaged the boat to make Eleanor's disappearance look accidental.
Someone else manipulated the boat and Adrian is being framed.
